skill.name: summon-daem0n
skill.description: Guides Daem0n-MCP setup for project memory, linked repositories, Claude hooks, and search tuning.
skill.summary: Configure Daem0n-MCP memory workflows across single and multi-repository projects.
skill.author: DasBluEyedDevil

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline tool names, and documentation examples. Confirmed risks remain around persistent Claude hook command execution, automatic memory capture, and a destructive hidden-directory cleanup command.

remediation.issue: Claude hooks execute Python scripts automatically from $HOME/Daem0nMCP.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before enabling hooks, document each script, and verify script paths and checksums before use.

remediation.issue: The guide includes a destructive rm -rf cleanup command for .daem0nmcp.
remediation.suggestion: Replace destructive deletion with a guarded cleanup workflow that checks the exact path, makes a backup, and asks for confirmation.

remediation.issue: Automatic memory capture may retain sensitive project or conversation details.
remediation.suggestion: Add consent, opt-out controls, retention limits, and clear storage documentation before enabling Silent Scribe behavior.

remediation.issue: Command examples use absolute placeholder paths such as /repos.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to adapt paths carefully and avoid running examples without reviewing the target directory.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The hook JSON directly invokes Python scripts on PreToolUse, PostToolUse, and Stop. These commands are triggered by AI tool activity and persist in Claude settings.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Session Memory Capture
semantic_findings.description: The skill says the Daem0n listens always, catches user words, and inscribes decisions automatically. That behavior can retain sensitive project context without explicit per-entry approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The prose describes always-on listening and automatic inscription, and the CLI example records decision content. The file does not show data exfiltration, so the risk is local retention and privacy exposure.

content.value_statement: Developers lose context when work spans repositories and sessions. This skill guides Daem0n-MCP setup for shared memory, linked projects, hooks, and search tuning.
actual_capabilities: Shows parent and linked setup patterns for related repositories.
Documents consolidation of child project memory databases.
Provides Claude hook settings for pre-edit, post-edit, and stop events.
Lists recall, search tuning, indexing, and health check options.
Describes backup and migration steps for existing Daem0n data.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not install Daem0n-MCP.
It assumes Daem0n-MCP commands and hook scripts already exist.
Examples use placeholder paths that users must adapt carefully.
Hook behavior depends on local scripts outside this skill.

use_cases.title: Set up one project memory store
use_cases.description: Use the skill to understand how Daem0n-MCP initializes memory for a single repository.

use_cases.title: Connect related repositories
use_cases.description: Plan shared or linked memory for client, server, and support repositories.

use_cases.title: Tune recall and indexing
use_cases.description: Review search, condensed recall, automatic tags, and health indicators for larger codebases.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize a single repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up Daem0n-MCP memory for this one repository. Explain the steps before suggesting any command.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a multi-repo layout
prompt_templates.prompt: I have related frontend and backend repositories. Compare parent memory and linked memory, then recommend one approach.

prompt_templates.title: Review an existing memory store
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my current Daem0n-MCP setup conceptually and propose a cautious migration plan with backup and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a guarded hook workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe Claude hook workflow for Daem0n-MCP. Include consent points, script review, and rollback steps.

output_examples.input: I have backend and client repositories under one parent folder.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends using the parent folder as the shared memory root when both repositories belong to one product.

output_examples.input: My existing memory folder is messy and may contain useful decisions.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests making a backup first, reviewing the stored context, and only deleting data after explicit confirmation.

output_examples.input: Recall returns too many long results for a broad topic.
output_examples.output: The skill points to condensed recall and search tuning so you can scan many memories before deeper review.

best_practices: Back up Daem0n-MCP data before consolidation or cleanup.
Review hook scripts before enabling automatic command execution.
Use one shared memory root for repositories that form one product.
anti_patterns: Do not run destructive cleanup commands without a verified backup.
Do not enable hooks from unreviewed local scripts.
Do not merge unrelated project memories into one store.

faq.question: Does this skill install Daem0n-MCP?
faq.answer: No. It explains setup patterns and assumes Daem0n-MCP is available in the environment.

faq.question: Can it support multiple repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents parent-directory memory and linked-project approaches for related repositories.

faq.question: Does it modify Claude settings?
faq.answer: It shows settings examples for hooks, but users should review scripts before enabling them.

faq.question: Can it delete project memory?
faq.answer: The guide includes a cleanup example. Users should back up data and confirm the target path first.

faq.question: Does it send data to a network service?
faq.answer: No network service is shown in the skill file. Hook scripts are external and need separate review.

faq.question: Is it useful with Codex and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
